newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 13.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- One senior government official said the conservative New Korea Party is considering a political meeting between President Kim Young-sam, and opposition party leaders Kim Dae-jung and Kim Jong-pil. Among the topics to be discussed are issues such as the present labour law, the nation's economy, Korea-Japan high-level talks, and a briefing on the four-party talks between South Korea, North Korea, the United States and China.

- Accordint to the government, there are too many car manufacturing companies causing an overlap in installation investment and an excess of production facilities. Therefore Seoul will call for a restructuring of the car manufacturing sector through possible mergers and acquisitions such as those already planned for the financial sector.

- The government and the ruling New Korea Party are working out a package of measures aimed at defusing the labour unrest situation. Senior officials ruled out the possibility of rewriting the labour bills any time before they take effect on March 1, but left open the possibility of an amendment thereafter.
